Collision checking along a path

Source: R/collision.R
robot_check_path.Rd

Checks the straight joint-space segments between consecutive waypoints.

Usage

robot_check_path(
  robot,
  path,
  environment = NULL,
  self = TRUE,
  resolution = 0.02,
  margin = 0,
  check_limits = TRUE,
  method = c("discrete", "continuous"),
  tol = 1e-09,
  max_steps = 10000
)

Arguments

robot

A robot_model with collision geometry.

path

Matrix of waypoints (one per row) or a robot_plan.

environment

Optional robot_environment.

self

Check self-collision.

resolution

Maximum joint step between checked samples (discrete method).

margin

Safety margin: pairs closer than margin count as colliding.

check_limits

Also require samples to respect joint limits.

method

"discrete" or "continuous".

tol

Clearance treated as contact by the continuous method.

max_steps

Maximum advancement steps per segment (continuous method); reaching it reports the segment as invalid with a warning.

Value

A list with valid, first_invalid (the index of the first invalid sample for the discrete method, or of the first invalid segment for the continuous method; NA when valid), the invalid configuration q, and samples, the number of configurations checked.

Details

With method = "discrete" (the default) each segment is sampled so that no joint moves more than resolution between samples (radians or meters). This can miss collisions with obstacles thinner than the swept motion between samples.

With method = "continuous" each segment is checked by conservative advancement: at the current configuration the clearance \(d\) of every geometry pair is computed, together with an upper bound \(M\) on how far any point of the pair can move per unit of the segment parameter (from the joint displacements and fixed bounds on the lever arms of the kinematic chain). Advancing by \(d / M\) cannot create a contact, so the motion is collision-free when the steps reach the end of the segment and in collision as soon as a clearance drops to margin. The test is exact for the continuous straight-line motion, up to tol; unbounded prismatic joints below a link make its bound infinite, and the check then fails with an error.

Examples

robot <- robot_capsule_links(robot_example("planar2"), 0.05)
env <- robot_environment(box = geom_box(c(0.4, 0.4, 0.4),
                                        origin = transl(1.5, 0, 0)))
robot_check_path(robot, rbind(c(pi / 2, 0), c(-pi / 2, 0)), env)$valid
#> [1] FALSE
